content: 1. Omaveloxolone reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. This interaction may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, including combination pills, patches, rings, implants, and progestin-only pills. It is recommended to avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If hormonal contraceptives are used, additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be employed. 2. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during co-administration. 3. Pentobarbital reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may compromise the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 4. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 15. Sugammadex sodium decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by competing for receptor binding. A bolus dose of sugammadex is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients should use additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods for the next 7 days after administration. 16. Tipranavir can cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, either increasing or decreasing them, by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 17. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be used. 18. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. If unavoidable, additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be used during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 19. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A substrates should be avoided. If unavoidable, the dose of CYP3A substrates should be reduced according to product labeling. 20. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics, such as albiglutide, by impairing glucose tolerance. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 21. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction may increase serum concentrations of benzodiazepines. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Concomitant use of ethinyl estradiol and aminocaproic acid may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Amoxicillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25.
